question: Given the same task, model, timeout, and starting commit, does mounting pack X as OpenCode skills produce a better observable result than mounting pack Y?

arms.lam: L.A.M. Stack v0.2.1 (git archive of tag)

mount: full pack tree at .pack/ inside the candidate workdir; opencode.json points skills at the pack's skill dirs; XDG_CONFIG_HOME is isolated so no user/global skills leak in
model_swap_rule: if a runner model produces no usable output on ANY arm in the pilot, it is replaced for the entire matrix before scoring; the replacement is recorded here before runs continue

judge.formula: blinded rubric, 4 criteria x 2.5 each, one judge model for all arms

floor_penalty.rules: lam floor-guard rule set applied to all arms equally

win_rule: LAM wins the duel iff median(composite_lam) > median(composite_rival) across the task x seed matrix AND median(acceptance_lam) >= median(acceptance_rival)
gate: LAM is GA-ready iff it wins >= 1 duel vs {pstack, pocock, osmani}; README claims must name which packs were beaten
noise_rule: a cell where BOTH arms produce zero diff is degenerate; if more than half of a model's cells are degenerate, the whole model matrix is rerun on the swap model

lanes.subagent_lane: added post-freeze, pre-result: same tasks/specs/grader on subagent_general (SWE-2-medium), skills mounted at .devin/skills/; saturates at 13.3-13.5/14 on all arms -> no separation at this model strength
lanes.opencode_lane: primary lane per spec; quota-blocked until ~2026-11-09T05:50Z; delayed matrix armed via setsid pid-file runs/opencode-delayed.log

efficiency.metric: total transcript tokens consumed per run (usage field in opencode --format json events)
efficiency.verdict_rule: if composite medians tie within a duel, LAM beats the rival iff median(eff_lam) > median(eff_rival) * 1.25; recorded before any opencode-lane result exists
